status.description: Which queue to list. Defaults to 'approved' - what the owner has greenlit and what builders take from.

type.description: Restrict to one item type. Omit to get every type.
guide = an article; tool = a free interactive widget; backlink = an outreach target; update = a change to an existing page.

title.description: The proposed page or tool title, as it would read on the site.

primary_keyword.description: The single keyword this item targets.

volume.description: Monthly search volume for primary_keyword, from the research source. Omit when the project has no volume data.

kd.description: Keyword difficulty (0-100) for primary_keyword, from the research source.

rationale.description: Why this is worth doing: volume, KD, intent, SERP weakness - and who types the query and why that person overlaps the site's buyer.

spec.description: Free-form brief. Guides: outline, angle, serp_notes. Tools: the intended functionality. Backlinks: the target url. A take grown from one viral post also carries seed_url (+ seed_stats).

source.description: Who queued it. Trend workflows MUST pass 'trend-scan'. 'manual' is ONLY for ideas the owner dictated in the current conversation - never from an autonomous run.

trend_topic_id.description: The trend topic this take belongs to - passed by trend-expand so each take groups under its subject on the radar.

approved.description: Manual ideas only: skip the pending gate and land straight in the build queue.

position.description: 'front' means do this one next - guides ship one per morning, so front means tomorrow. Defaults to back.

build.description: Tools only: 'now' fires the tool builder immediately instead of waiting for the weekly build. Never pass 'now' from an autonomous run.

id.description: The suggestion's id, as returned by get_suggestions.

status.description: The new status. Builders set 'in_progress' when they start and 'done' when the PR is open.

result_pr_url.description: The pull request this item produced. Pass it alongside status 'done'.

decided_by.description: Pass 'owner' ONLY when the site owner made the call in the current conversation ('approve that one'). Never from an autonomous workflow run.

group.description: Which queue to reorder - guides and tools are ordered independently.

ordered_ids.description: Every suggestion id in this group, in the new build order, first to last.

id.description: The suggestion to build immediately, as returned by get_suggestions.

keyword.description: The new guide's primary keyword, used to rank internal-link candidates by topical closeness. Omit on the first call if the queue head is what tells you the keyword.

markdown.description: The full draft to check, as markdown.

primary_keyword.description: The keyword this draft targets, so the check can weigh it against pages already covering it.

stage.description: 'final' (the default) is the full pre-publish gate on the finished draft - unchanged. 'outline' is the cheap EARLY probe: pass just the planned opening line plus the H2 headings as markdown, BEFORE drafting prose or building visuals, and it checks the two signals an outline can carry (opening word-run, heading skeleton). Catching a collision here costs a replanned outline instead of a discarded draft. It skips the stock-phrase signal, which needs body prose, so an outline pass NEVER substitutes for the final check - always run 'final' on the finished guide before the PR.

suggestion_id.description: The queued idea this article fulfils (from get_suggestions / get_build_brief). Omit only for an article the owner asked for that was never in the queue.

title.description: The article title as it should appear on the page.

slug.description: URL slug, lowercase and hyphenated, no leading or trailing slash - e.g. 'how-to-price-a-service'.

meta_description.description: Meta description, roughly 120-160 characters. Omitted means we build one from the opening.

primary_keyword.description: The single search term this article targets, exactly as someone would type it.

markdown.description: The full article in markdown. No frontmatter, no raw HTML, no code fences wrapping the whole thing.

question.description: The question, phrased as a real question ending in '?'.

answer.description: The answer in a couple of full sentences - at least 8 words, never a stub.

faq.description: Real Q&A pairs for the FAQ block and its schema. Each question ends in '?' and each answer is a couple of sentences, not a stub.

url.description: The source's full URL, including https://.

title.description: The source page or publication's title.

sources.description: External sources you actually used, as full URLs. Placeholder or example.com URLs fail the gate.

cover_brief.description: Optional one-line description of the cover image's subject. Never published as text.

status.description: Only this status. Omit for everything, newest first.

limit.description: How many to return, newest first. Defaults to 20.

id.description: The draft id from get_drafts or submit_article.
The draft id from get_drafts or submit_article.

suggestion_id.description: The queued idea this research is for. Omit for research the owner asked for that is not tied to a queued idea.

notes.description: Your findings as a JSON object - serp, gaps, angle, outline, sources, whatever the work produced. Up to 64KB.

suggestion_id.description: The queued idea whose notes you want. Omit to list recent unattached notes.

target.description: Where finished articles go from now on.

path.description: Repo-relative folder, e.g. content/blog. Empty string clears the hint.

keyword.description: The search term to track, exactly as a user would type it.

volume.description: Monthly search volume from the research source. Never estimate it.

kd.description: Keyword difficulty, 0-100, from the research source.

cpc.description: Cost per click in USD, from the research source.

intent.description: Search intent for this term, e.g. informational, commercial, transactional.

keywords.description: One entry per keyword to start tracking. Send the whole batch in a single call.

keyword.description: Restrict to one tracked keyword. Omit for every tracked keyword.

days.description: How far back to read rank history, in days.

url.description: The page's full public URL on the site.

type.description: What kind of page this is.

primary_keyword.description: The keyword this page targets - the same one its suggestion carried.

pr_url.description: The pull request that shipped this page.

published_at.description: Publication date as YYYY-MM-DD. Take it from running `date -u +%F` in the shell, never from memory.

requested_urls.description: URLs indexing was just requested for, so they aren't re-submitted on the next run.

already_indexed_urls.description: URLs found to be indexed already, so they drop out of the queue without a request being spent.

days.description: How many days of history to summarise.

domain.description: The prospect site's domain, without protocol or www.

url.description: The specific page to pitch - a submission form, a resource list, a relevant article.

reason.description: Why this site would plausibly link here: what it already covers, and the angle to pitch.

domain_rating.description: The prospect's domain rating (0-100) from the research source. Never estimate it.

status.description: Filter to one stage. Omit to get every prospect.

id.description: The prospect's id, as returned by get_backlink_prospects.

status.description: Where this prospect now stands: contacted after outreach, acquired once the link is live.

keyword.description: The search term to fetch a live SERP for, exactly as a user would type it.

top.description: How many results to return, up to 100. Defaults to a shallow page-one read.

engine.description: Which AI engine produced this answer.

query.description: The customer question exactly as it was asked.

has_ai_answer.description: Whether the engine produced an AI answer at all, as opposed to plain links or nothing.

cited.description: Whether this site was among the answer's cited sources.

cited_url.description: Which URL of this site was cited. Pass it whenever cited is true.

answer_excerpt.description: A verbatim excerpt of the answer. Copy it exactly - never paraphrase or summarise.

title.description: The cited source's title as the engine showed it.

citations.description: Every source the answer cited, in the order shown - including competitors, which is how gap domains are found.

results.description: One entry per question asked. Send the whole scan in a single call, not one call per question.

seed.description: The base term to build variations from.

modifiers.description: Words to combine with the seed, e.g. 'free', 'vs', 'for teams', 'alternative'.

seeds.description: Seed keywords to expand from, BEST FIRST - only the first 5 are actually expanded (2 metered calls each), the rest are skipped and named in the response note.

limit.description: Maximum ideas to return, up to 200, after merging and deduping both endpoints across all expanded seeds.

name.description: The site or product name as it should appear in a directory listing.

tagline.description: One short line summarising the product, 60 characters or fewer.

short_description.description: One or two sentences, 160 characters or fewer - the blurb most directories ask for.

long_description.description: A fuller description between 100 and 700 characters, for directories with a longer field.

categories.description: One to five categories the product belongs to.

tags.description: One to ten keywords describing the product.

site_url.description: The Search Console property to track, exactly as Search Console lists it (e.g. 'sc-domain:example.com' or 'https://example.com/').

location_code.description: DataForSEO location code from the supported list, e.g. 2840 = United States, 2376 = Israel.

language_code.description: Language code the chosen market supports, e.g. 'en', 'he', 'de'.

confirm.description: The connected repo as owner/name, typed exactly. Guards against a disconnect nobody asked for.

repo.description: The repository as owner/name (a github.com URL is accepted too).

agent.description: claude = Claude Code (Runs on your existing Claude subscription - nothing extra to pay, and nothing is billed by DispatchSEO.); codex = Codex (Runs on your own OpenAI API key - OpenAI bills you per run, and nothing is billed by DispatchSEO.); cursor = Cursor (Runs on your Cursor plan - nothing is billed by DispatchSEO. Any plan can mint the builder's API key; builds draw on the plan's included usage, so the free pool may not last a nightly schedule.)

enabled.description: true to allow editing published posts, false to stop

job.description: The cron job key to clear, as reported by get_cron_health.

number.description: The pull request number to merge.

limit.description: How many of the most recent releases to return, up to 50.
How many requests to return, most-voted first.

title.description: The request in one line, up to 120 characters.

body.description: Optional detail: what you're trying to do and what gets in the way.

vote.description: true to vote (default), false to take the vote back.

hidden.description: true hides it from the board, false puts it back.

slug.description: Fetch one playbook step by slug. Omit for the whole playbook.
The playbook step's slug, as returned by get_playbook.

status.description: Where this step stands: 'skipped' means deliberately not doing it, not failed.

title.description: The subject in a few words, as it should read on the dashboard's Trend radar.

why_now.description: Why this is worth writing about THIS week - the timeliness argument, not a general description.

signals.description: What proves the topic is moving right now: engagement numbers, velocity, repeated discussion.

sources.description: URLs the signals came from, so the owner can judge the evidence.

seed_url.description: The one specific post or video this topic grew from. Takes built on it credit and quote it directly.

seed_stats.description: The seed's traction at scan time, e.g. '4.2k upvotes, 380 comments in 2 days'.

status.description: Filter the radar to one stage. Omit for every topic.

id.description: The trend topic's id, as returned by get_trend_topics.

status.description: 'expanded' once takes have been queued from it; 'dismissed' to drop it off the radar.

id.description: The trend topic to expand into takes, as returned by get_trend_topics.

workflow.description: Which playbook to fetch. Call this FIRST in every run - it overrides any cached knowledge of the pipeline.

path.description: Return a single file from the pipeline pack by its repo-relative path. Omit for every file.

step.description: Which install step just completed. Stamps it on the dashboard's live setup checklist.

product_summary.description: What the product does, in a few sentences - the grounding every research and build run reads first.
